**VERDICT: PARTIALLY TRUE.** As of **2026-10-30**, I found **no verified Class A source** reporting genome-wide, per-gene medium attribution—with catalogue-wide fractions—for the two specified 2026 organoid dependency catalogues. That narrow contribution remains defensible. The surrounding framing is overstated, however: Neiswender already includes genome-wide format comparisons; earlier large-scale dependency studies quantify medium associations; Sanger explicitly documents a genome-wide correction for medium-associated variation; and a 2025 conference abstract reports genome-scale serum-containing versus serum-free CRISPR comparisons. The manuscript should claim a **systematic medium-consistency audit of these particular catalogues**, rather than an unprecedented genome-wide separation of medium and format. Relevant precedents include [Neiswender](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10843-7), [Lagziel](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12915-019-0654-4), [Pacini](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-21898-7), and [Liang](https://doi.org/10.1093/neuped/wuaf001.127).

This is a novelty and interpretation audit. I read the manuscript from disk, but did **not** independently reproduce its numerical results.

**Evidence table**

**A:** the specified catalogue-wide attribution, directly falsifying the narrow claim.  
**B:** substantial overlap requiring narrower novelty wording.  
**C:** adjacent or distinct evidence.

“No catalogue fraction found” below describes the material inspected, not proof that an inaccessible supplement contains none.

| Source | Year | Scale | Quantified what / relevance | Class | DOI / URL |
|---|---:|---|---|:---:|---|
| **Neiswender et al., “A dependency map enhanced with next-generation 3D cancer models”** | 2026 | 147 genome-scale NextGen screens; additional selected-gene experiments | Genome-wide format comparisons and selected medium/format effects. No catalogue-wide medium-attribution fraction located. Important omitted precedent; details below. | **B** | [10.1038/s41586-026-10843-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10843-7) |
| **Broad NextGen released data and analysis code** | 2026 | Genome-wide comparison outputs; 1,000-gene minipool | Separate medium and format coefficient/test tables for the minipool; genome-wide format-analysis code. No inspected genome-wide catalogue medium-attribution flags. | **B** | [10.6084/m9.figshare.29472362](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.29472362); [code](https://github.com/broadinstitute/DepMap-NextGen-Public) |
| **Herranz-Ors et al., “A tumour-derived organoid biobank maps cancer gene dependencies”** | 2026 | 162 screened organoids; 97 organoid-exclusive core genes; 18 highlighted genes | Organoid-specific essentiality, selected growth-factor experiments, and differences in fitness-gene calls. No medium-attribution fraction located. | **B** | [10.1038/s41586-026-10830-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10830-y) |
| **Sanger organoid supplementary tables and code** | 2026 | Ten supplementary tables, including genome-wide calls and fold changes | Inspected table schemas cover screen QC, fitness calls, differential dependencies, biomarkers and drugs; no medium-attribution field located. | **B**, supporting original study | [10.6084/m9.figshare.28339340](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.28339340); [code](https://github.com/Garnett-Lab/SangerOrganoidBiobank) |
| **Zaidi & Sawyers, “Expanding DepMap: is the juice worth the squeeze?”** | 2026 | Commentary on the Nature studies | Explicitly questions whether steroid/isoprenoid dependencies reflect culture conditions. No numerical medium share. **This is the same source as candidate s41422-026-01311-y.** | **B**, interpretive overlap | [10.1038/s41422-026-01311-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41422-026-01311-y) |
| **Liang et al., METB-03, “CRISPR screens in serum-free medium reveal conditionally essential genes in Paediatric CNS tumours”** | 2025 | Genome-scale Cas12a comparisons in CNS tumour models; model count unspecified in abstract | Serum-containing versus serum-free screens; cholesterol-biosynthesis dependencies emerge under serum-free conditions. No released gene table or fraction identified. Published conference abstract, not a demonstrated hundreds-model catalogue. | **B** | [10.1093/neuped/wuaf001.127](https://doi.org/10.1093/neuped/wuaf001.127) |
| **Metz et al., “Variation in guide RNA library representation results in gene effect score bias in genome-wide CRISPR screens”** | 2026 | 20 screens across four cell lines; Humagne C/D; HPLM versus DMEM | Genome-wide medium and library comparisons. **Both media contain 10% FBS**; this is not serum-free versus serum-containing. Library effects substantially complicate interpretation. | **B** | [10.1186/s12864-026-12658-2](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12864-026-12658-2) |
| **Lagziel, Lee & Shlomi, “Inferring cancer dependencies on metabolic genes from large-scale genetic screens”** | 2019 | 501 RNAi and 341 CRISPR cell lines | Among selected highly variable metabolic genes, **22/59 (37%) RNAi and 15/58 (26%) CRISPR** dependencies associated with DMEM/RPMI. These denominators are neither all genes nor organoid-specific hits. Strong precedent for quantified medium associations. | **B** | [10.1186/s12915-019-0654-4](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12915-019-0654-4) |
| **Joly et al., “The landscape of metabolic pathway dependencies in cancer cell lines”** | 2021 | Genome-wide dependency input; metabolic pathway analyses across CCLE/DepMap models | Compares medium and adherent/suspension contexts; identifies medium-associated metabolic pathway dependencies. No organoid-catalogue attribution. | **B** | [10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008942](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008942) |
| **Pacini et al., “Integrated cross-study datasets of genetic dependencies in cancer”** | 2021 | 908 cell lines; 17,486 genes | Benchmarks integration pipelines including principal-component removal. Metabolic enrichment of the removed component is interpreted as consistent with medium differences; not a causally isolated medium component. | **B** | [10.1038/s41467-021-21898-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-21898-7) |
| **Official Sanger processing documentation** | Current in 2026 | Integrated genome-wide cell-line dependency data | Explicitly documents removing PC1 associated with medium differences. The separately described organoid pipeline does not supply catalogue-wide medium attribution. | **B** | [Genome-scale knockout documentation](https://depmap.sanger.ac.uk/documentation/datasets/wg-crispr-knockout/) |
| **Dempster et al., “Agreement between two large pan-cancer CRISPR-Cas9 gene dependency data sets”** | 2019 | Large Broad/Sanger genome-wide comparison | Investigates medium-associated ASNS differences and screen-duration effects on late-depleting essentials. Important precedent for both medium confounding and depletion dynamics. | **B** | [10.1038/s41467-019-13805-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-13805-y) |
| **Rossiter et al., “CRISPR screens in physiologic medium reveal conditionally essential genes in human cells”** | 2021 | Genome-wide K562 discovery; focused follow-up across conditions/models | Per-gene medium-dependent essentiality, nutrient complementation and serum-treatment comparisons. Already acknowledged by the manuscript. | **B**, known precedent | [10.1016/j.cmet.2021.02.005](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cmet.2021.02.005) |
| **Han et al., “CRISPR screens in cancer spheroids identify 3D growth-specific vulnerabilities”** | 2020 | Genome-wide 2D/spheroid screens | Quantified format-associated dependencies. Does not attribute the 2026 organoid catalogues to medium. | **B** | [10.1038/s41586-020-2099-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2099-x) |
| **Price et al., organoid suspension-screening study** | 2022 | Genome-scale 18,009-gene screen in COLO-027; broader culture-method evaluation | Compares BME dome and suspension screening; genome-wide matrix/format precedent. | **B** | [10.1038/s41598-022-09508-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-022-09508-y) |

The remaining verified candidates and useful mechanistic context are distinct from the claimed attribution:

| Source | Year | Scale | Quantified what / relevance | Class | DOI / URL |
|---|---:|---|---|:---:|---|
| **ElHarouni et al., “A compendium of next-generation patient-derived models for diverse cancers”** | 2026 | 665 models; extensive molecular profiling | Culture-associated transcriptional states and model fidelity; not a genome-wide dependency decomposition. | **C** | [10.1038/s41586-026-10806-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10806-y) |
| **Fırat & Kılıçaslan, transferability analysis — candidate PMC13664187** | 2026 | **20 preselected genes**, 852 cell lines, 94 Broad and 148 Sanger organoids | Cross-system transferability of selected dependencies. Reuses both catalogues, but neither genome-wide nor a medium-attribution analysis. | **C** | [10.3390/biology15191782](https://doi.org/10.3390/biology15191782); [PMC13664187](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13664187/) |
| **Yeo et al., “Serum albumin maintains Wnt3a water solubility and activity”** | 2026 | Biochemical, reporter and organoid assays | Albumin-dependent Wnt3a availability/activity. Relevant formulation mechanism; no dependency catalogue. | **C** | [10.1038/s42003-026-11202-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-026-11202-y) |
| **Eaton et al., “Commonly used organoid culture media prevent ferroptosis”** | 2024 preprint | Pathway-focused organoid/media experiments | Antioxidant-containing media can suppress ferroptosis phenotypes. Metadata and abstract verified; complete preprint not retrieved. | **C** | [10.1101/2024.04.29.591759](https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.04.29.591759) |
| **Chan et al., “A combined enteric neuron-gastric tumor organoid reveals metabolic vulnerabilities in gastric cancer”** | 2025 | Genome-wide discovery in one gastric PDO; focused follow-up | Identifies metabolic vulnerabilities including LSS/ACACA and examines neuronal influences. No catalogue-wide medium/format attribution identified. Full large PDF was not completely retrieved. | **C** | [10.1016/j.stem.2025.08.006](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.stem.2025.08.006) |
| **Zhu et al., “Functional Genomics In Vivo Reveal Metabolic Dependencies of Pancreatic Cancer Cells”** | 2020 online / 2021 issue | Metabolism-focused in-vitro/in-vivo screening | Heme synthesis becomes important **in vivo**, with increased heme degradation implicated. **What most strongly challenges the framing**

1. **The original Broad study already performs genome-wide format analysis.** Extended Data Fig. 4g–h compares 55 dome-grown with 14 coat-grown organoids: correlation 0.984, with all differential-test q-values above 0.71. These are unmatched model groups. Fig. 5h/Extended Data Fig. 10a individually validate MSMO1 and SQLE effects. The paper also discusses lost ESR1/ERBB2 dependencies. Consequently, neither genome-wide format comparison nor attention to dependency losses is new here. [Neiswender et al.](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10843-7)

2. **The minipool denominator matters.** The released materials distinguish 250 selected test genes from 650 negative and 100 positive controls. Counting significant entries in the released test tables gives eight medium-associated genes—PTK2, SPTLC1, CTNNA1, SPTLC2, PPP1R15B, RICTOR, SQLE and PPP2R2D—and seven format-associated genes. That is **not** a fraction of all organoid-specific dependencies. MSMO1 is supported by the separate validation assays, rather than significant minipool regression. The medium contrast changes whole formulations, OPAC versus RPMI–FBS; it does not isolate serum alone. [Released data](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.29472362)

3. **Genome-wide medium-associated correction is established resource practice.** Sanger’s documentation explicitly describes removal of a medium-associated principal component from integrated **cell-line** data. This must be credited, while recognizing that PC removal neither identifies a purely causal medium component nor supplies the proposed organoid target flags. [Sanger documentation](https://depmap.sanger.ac.uk/documentation/datasets/wg-crispr-knockout/), [Pacini et al.](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-21898-7)

4. **Serum-free genome-scale comparisons exist beyond Rossiter.** Liang is a direct precedent, but its abstract does not establish catalogue scale or publish attribution fractions. Metz supplies another genome-wide medium comparison, with serum present in both conditions. I found no verified hundreds-model factorial serum/serum-free catalogue matching the proposed analysis. [Liang et al.](https://doi.org/10.1093/neuped/wuaf001.127), [Metz et al.](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12864-026-12658-2)

**An unreliable publication claim encountered during the hunt**

A public Zannix Labs pancreatic-dependency report combines a genome-wide organoid/cell-line comparison with medium/format regression. Its regression is explicitly restricted to the **250 minipool test genes**, so its scope is **B at most**, not A. However, its advertised arXiv-style identifier, `2610.10843`, resolves to an unrelated paper. The website/PDF exists; the claimed publication identity is not reliable. I exclude its scientific conclusions and claimed publication status from the verdict basis. [Report](https://www.zannixlabs.com/research/depmap-pancreatic-dependencies?view=original), [PDF](https://www.zannixlabs.com/papers/depmap-pancreatic-dependencies.pdf), [actual arXiv record](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10843)

Locations refer to [manuscript_draft_v2.md](/Users/bmarti44/github/bufferright/research/cancer-dependency-rsi/manuscript/manuscript_draft_v2.md).

The background corrections are supported by the formulation and context studies above, particularly [Seghers](https://doi.org/10.1186/s40164-026-00831-y), [Yeo](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-026-11202-y), [Zhu](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cmet.2020.10.017), and [Kubota](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.molmet.2024.101964).

Two statements outside the requested Abstract/Introduction also materially affect the novelty argument:

- **Results: “Neither 2026 catalogue reports or adjusts for the weakening…”** This is too broad. Sanger reports fewer fitness-gene calls in organoids—median 1,440 versus 2,507 in cell lines—and discusses screen-score differences. Existing pipelines also apply essential/nonessential scaling or growth-related modelling. Restrict the claim to **the specific residual ribosomal pattern after the manuscript’s stated adjustments**, if that is what the evidence establishes. [Herranz-Ors](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10830-y), [Chronos](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-021-02540-7)
- **Discussion: nutrient-synthesis dependencies “should be treated as medium-consistent until tested under repletion.”** Pathway membership alone does not establish that classification. Prefer **“should be prioritized for matched medium-switch and nutrient-repletion tests.”** Heme and mevalonate/GGPP dependencies can remain important in vivo. [Zhu](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cmet.2020.10.017), [Kubota](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.molmet.2024.101964)

A compact replacement novelty statement is:

> **Building on previous analyses of medium- and format-associated dependencies, we systematically audit the two 2026 organoid dependency catalogues. We report per-gene medium-consistency classifications and the fractions of published dependency gains and losses meeting prespecified criteria. These observational classifications do not causally partition medium and format effects. To our knowledge, this catalogue-wide annotation has not previously been reported.**

Forward citation chasing found a substantive critical commentary, a selected-gene transferability reanalysis, and unrelated citing work. It did **not** reveal a verified genome-wide medium-share reanalysis. Relevant examples are [Zaidi/Sawyers](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41422-026-01311-y), [Fırat/Kılıçaslan](https://doi.org/10.3390/biology15191782), and [Yasar et al.](https://doi.org/10.3390/life16101752).

**Saturation point:** after identifying the Sanger/Pacini correction precedent, repeated attribution-, fraction-, correction-, author-, repository- and citation-focused searches stopped producing new A/B sources. Later new results concerned individual pathways, drug responses, general organoid methods or unrelated citing papers. I therefore reached **practical saturation for publicly discoverable evidence bearing on the narrow novelty claim**, not universal saturation of all organoid literature.

**Coverage limits and confidence**

- Both Nature papers were inspected using accessible web material and local copies of their primary full-text XML.
- Supplementary data inspection included cached primary Broad files and the Sanger ten-table archive. **Not every supplementary spreadsheet cell was audited.**
- Some supplementary narrative and peer-review PDFs could not be retrieved. Complete text was also unavailable for selected preprints and the large gastric-organoid PDF; these limitations constrain negative conclusions about their contents.
- Citation chasing used indexed DOI/title references. A complete forward-citation export was not obtained from citation APIs.
- Very recent October publications, unindexed repositories, private analyses and unpublished work remain potential gaps.
- **High confidence:** several broad novelty interpretations are overstated.
- **Moderate confidence:** the specific catalogue-wide fractions and per-gene medium-consistency annotation remain unreported in discoverable literature through **2026-10-30**.
- **No basis for absolute priority language:** use **“to our knowledge”**, retain the observational limitation, and describe the distinct deliverable precisely.
